title: Tangents & normals
examples: How do I find the gradient of the tangent at a specific point?
If I know the gradient of the tangent, how do I find the normal?
What is the relationship between the tangent and the normal line?

explain.say: Today we learn about tangents and normals to curves. First we find the gradient at a point. You need the derivative for this calculation.

items: Step 2: Evaluate derivative at point 'a' to get gradient (m)

draw.text: Gradient at a Point: y' (a) x=a

explain.say: If the gradient of the curve at point a is m, then m equals the derivative evaluated at a. For example, if y equals x squared, the derivative is two x. At x equals three, the gradient is two times three, which is six.

draw.text: Example: y=x², y'=2x. Gradient at x=3 is 6.

explain.say: Next we find the normal line. The normal is perpendicular to the tangent at that point. Its gradient is the negative reciprocal of the tangent's gradient.
So if the tangent gradient is six, the normal gradient is negative one divided by six. This is a key rule to remember for normals.

items: Remember this key rule for normals

faq.q: What is the negative reciprocal of a gradient?
faq.a: It means you flip the fraction and change the sign. For example, the negative reciprocal of three divided by four is negative four divided by three.
asks: How do I find the negative reciprocal?
What is the reciprocal and then change the sign?

faq.q: Do I need the point coordinates to find the gradient?
faq.a: Yes, you must know the x value or the y value of the point. The derivative gives a formula, but you need the point to get the number.
asks: Can I find the gradient without a point?
Do I substitute the point into the derivative?

faq.q: If the tangent is horizontal, what is the normal?
faq.a: A horizontal tangent has a gradient of zero. The normal line will then be a vertical line, which has an undefined gradient.
asks: What happens if the gradient is zero?
If the tangent is flat, what is the normal?

faq.q: What if the normal is horizontal?
faq.a: If the normal is horizontal, its gradient is zero. This means the original tangent must have been a vertical line, which is unusual in these problems.
asks: Can the normal have a gradient of zero?
When is the normal line horizontal?

faq.q: Do I use the point-slope form for the normal equation?
faq.a: Yes, once you have the normal gradient and the point, use the point-slope form: y minus y equals m times x minus x.
asks: What form do I use for the final equation?
How do I write the equation for the normal?

facts: The gradient of the tangent at a point is found by evaluating the derivative at that point.
The normal line is always perpendicular to the tangent line at the point of contact.
If the tangent gradient is m, the normal gradient is negative one divided by m.
A horizontal line has a gradient of zero, and a vertical line has an undefined gradient.

quiz.say: The gradient of the tangent to y equals x squared plus one at x equals two is:
quiz.why: The derivative of x squared plus one is two x. Substituting two for x gives two times two, which is four.

wrong.1: This is the coefficient of x, but you must substitute the value of x into the derivative.
wrong.2: This is the result of x squared plus one, which is the y-value, not the gradient.
wrong.3: This is the constant term, and the derivative of a constant is zero, not one.

quiz.say: If the tangent gradient at a point is three divided by four, what is the gradient of the normal?
quiz.why: The negative reciprocal of three divided by four is negative four divided by three.

wrong.0: You only found the reciprocal but forgot to change the sign to negative.
wrong.1: You correctly took the negative sign but forgot to flip the fraction when finding the reciprocal.
wrong.3: You forgot to take the negative sign, which is required for the normal.

quiz.say: A curve has a tangent gradient of negative one at the point (1, 5). What is the gradient of the normal line?
quiz.why: The normal gradient is the negative reciprocal of negative one. This equals negative one divided by negative one, which is one.

wrong.1: You only took the negative sign but forgot to flip the fraction.
wrong.2: You correctly found the reciprocal but forgot to change the sign to negative.
wrong.3: This would only be the case if the tangent line was vertical, which is not the case here.
